## Full Rule Details (for reference)

- **CHG-001** [DEFINITIVE] Higher oxidation state of central atom → higher stretching frequency for the same molecular type [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **ENV-001** [DEFINITIVE] Hydrogen bonding: lowers X-H stretching frequency (broadens band), raises X-H bending frequency [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **FRQ-001** [DEFINITIVE] Bond order-frequency correlation: Higher bond order → higher vibrational frequency [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-001** [DEFINITIVE] O-H stretching: free OH ~3600-3700 cm⁻¹; H-bonded OH ~3400-3200 cm⁻¹ (broad); O-H bending ~1600-1650 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-002** [DEFINITIVE] N-H stretching: ~3300-3400 cm⁻¹ (NH₃ gas: ν₁ 3414, ν₃ 3336 cm⁻¹); N-H bending: ~1600-1650 cm⁻¹ (ν₂), ~930-970 cm⁻¹ (ν₄) [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-003** [DEFINITIVE] C-H stretching: ~2900-3100 cm⁻¹; C-H bending: ~1300-1500 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-004** [DEFINITIVE] Si-H stretching: ~2100-2200 cm⁻¹; Si-H bending: ~900-1000 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-018** [DEFINITIVE] O₂ molecule: ν(O-O) decreases with increasing negative charge: O₂⁺ (1876) > O₂ (1580) > O₂⁻ (1094) > O₂²⁻ (791/736 cm⁻¹) [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-022** [DEFINITIVE] ν(NO₂) for nitro/nitrite groups: NO₂⁻ (nitrite) νₐ 1327/1286, δ 806 cm⁻¹; NO₂ (neutral) νₐ 1610, νₛ 1325, δ 752 cm⁻¹; NO₂⁺ (nitronium) ν₃ 2360, ν₁ 1396 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-034** [DEFINITIVE] BF₃ (planar D3h): ν₁ 888 (Raman), ν₂ 719 (IR), ν₃ 1506 (IR+Raman), ν₄ 481 (IR+Raman) cm⁻¹. BCl₃: ν₁ 473, ν₂ ~950, ν₃ 951, ν₄ 254 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-035** [DEFINITIVE] PF₃ (pyramidal C3v): ν₁ 893, ν₂ 487, ν₃ 858, ν₄ 346 cm⁻¹. PCl₃: ν₁ 515, ν₂ 258, ν₃ 504, ν₄ 186 cm⁻¹. Trend: ν₁ > ν₃ and ν₂ > ν₄ for halogeno compounds (opposite to hydrides) [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-036** [DEFINITIVE] AsF₃ (pyramidal C3v): ν₁ 739, ν₂ 337, ν₃ 699, ν₄ 262 cm⁻¹. AsCl₃: ν₁ 417, ν₂ 193, ν₃ 391, ν₄ 150 cm⁻¹. ν(SbCl₃): ν₁ 381, ν₃ 359, ν₄ 122 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-037** [DEFINITIVE] BF₄⁻ (tetrahedral): ν₁ 777, ν₂ 360, ν₃ 1070, ν₄ 533 cm⁻¹. BCl₄⁻: ν₁ 406, ν₂ 192, ν₃ 722, ν₄ 278 cm⁻¹. ν₃ strongly halogen-dependent [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-038** [DEFINITIVE] NH₄⁺ (tetrahedral Td): ν₁ 3040, ν₂ 1680, ν₃ 3145, ν₄ 1400 cm⁻¹. ν(NH₄⁺) decreases with weaker H-bonding to counterion (F→Cl→Br→I) [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-039** [DEFINITIVE] CH₄: ν₁ 2917, ν₂ 1534, ν₃ 3019, ν₄ 1306 cm⁻¹. SiH₄: ν₁ 2180, ν₂ 970, ν₃ 2183, ν₄ 910 cm⁻¹. GeH₄: ν₁ 2106, ν₂ 931, ν₃ 2114, ν₄ 819 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-041** [DEFINITIVE] ν(M-Cl) in octahedral MCl₆ⁿ⁻: general order ν₁ > ν₃, ν₄ > ν₅ > ν₆. Representative: SF₆ ν₁ 775, ν₃ 939 cm⁻¹; UF₆ ν₁ 667, ν₃ 628 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-042** [DEFINITIVE] PF₅ (trigonal-bipyramidal D3h): equatorial ν₅(E′) 944, axial ν₃(A₂″) 575, ν₁(A₁′) 817, ν₂(A₁′) 740 cm⁻¹. Equatorial > axial trend [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-046** [DEFINITIVE] CCl₄: ν₁ 460, ν₂ 214, ν₃ 792/765, ν₄ 314 cm⁻¹. CF₄: ν₁ 908, ν₂ 435, ν₃ 1283, ν₄ 631 cm⁻¹. CBr₄: ν₁ 267, ν₂ 123, ν₃ 672, ν₄ 183 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-061** [DEFINITIVE] Diamond: single sharp Raman band at 1332 cm⁻¹ (F₂g). IR absorptions: type I ~2000 + ~1200 cm⁻¹ (N₂ defects + multiphonon), type II ~2000 cm⁻¹ only [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-069** [DEFINITIVE] H₂O₂: ν(OH) 3607/3608, ν(OO) 1394, δ(HOO) 864/1266, torsion 317 cm⁻¹. H₂O₂ nonplanar C2 with dihedral ~90° [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **ISO-001** [DEFINITIVE] Isotope shifts in diatomic molecules: ν(HX)/ν(DX) ≈ √2 ≈ 1.414 for hydrides/deuterides [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **SPC-002** [DEFINITIVE] Fermi resonance: when a fundamental and overtone/combination have similar frequencies and same symmetry, they mix and split. The higher-frequency band gains intensity [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GEO-016** [EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED] Square-planar X₄²⁺ cations (D4h): 6 normal modes classified into A1g(R)+B1g(R)+B2g(R)+B2u(inactive)+Eu(IR). Characteristic frequency ranges for S₄²⁺, Se₄²⁺, Te₄²⁺ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-015** [EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED] Fullerene C₆₀ characteristic modes: IR-active at 1428, 1182, 577, 527 cm⁻¹; Raman-active pentagonal pinching mode (A_g) at 1469 cm⁻¹, radial breathing (A_g) at 496 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-032** [DEFINITIVE] CS₂: ν₁ (Raman) 658, ν₂ (IR) 397, ν₃ (IR) 1533 cm⁻¹. COS: ν₁ 859, ν₂ 520, ν₃ 2062 cm⁻¹. CSe₂: ν₁ 369, ν₂ 313, ν₃ 1302 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-055** [EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED] ν(Mo=O): terminal at 940-930 cm⁻¹, ν(Mo-Mo) at 200-150 cm⁻¹ in Mo₆O₁₉²⁻ derivatives. ν(O-O) of side-on peroxide: 885 and 550 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **SEL-010** [EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED] Icosahedral C₆₀ (Ih): only 4 F₁u vibrations are IR-active; only 2 A_g and 8 H_g vibrations are Raman-active. Mutual exclusion rule holds [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **SPC-010** [EXPERIMENTALLY_VERIFIED] Isotopic fine structure in C₆₀: natural ¹³C (1.11%) gives 51% ¹²C₆₀, 35% ¹²C₅₉¹³C, 11% ¹²C₅₈¹³C₂. The pentagonal pinching A_g mode splits into 1471, 1470, 1469 cm⁻¹ peaks [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-027** [DEFINITIVE] CO₃²⁻ (carbonate, planar D3h): IR-active ν₂ 879 (CaCO₃ calcite), ν₃ 1429-1492, ν₄ 706 cm⁻¹. Raman: ν₁ 1087, ν₃ 1432, ν₄ 714 cm⁻¹ [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
- **GFQ-062** [DEFINITIVE] Graphite: single Raman band at 1575 cm⁻¹ (E₂g). No IR bands (D6h symmetry). ν(RBM) of SWNT ~186 cm⁻¹ for d~1.4 nm, inversely proportional to diameter [source: nakamoto2008infrared]
